questions.prompt: Complete the suggestion: "Why don't we ___ the bus to the beach?"
questions.explanation: "Why don't we" is followed by the bare verb: Why don't we take the bus to the beach? "taking" is the form that follows "What about"; "to take" adds a "to" this opener never takes, and "took" is a past form.

questions.prompt: Complete the suggestion: "I suggest that we ___ to the swimming pool."
questions.explanation: "I suggest that" is followed by a full clause, subject + verb: I suggest that we go to the swimming pool. "going" belongs after "What about"; "to go" is not a verb with a subject; "goes" does not agree with "we".

questions.prompt: Complete the suggestion: "Shall we ___ a picnic on the beach?"
questions.explanation: "Shall we" is followed by the bare verb, like "Let's" and "Why don't we": Shall we have a picnic on the beach? "having" is the -ing form of "What about"; "to have" and "had" are not bare verbs.

questions.prompt: Yesterday Sami was ill and missed his friend's party. Which sentence expresses his regret correctly?

options.text: I regret to missing your party.

questions.explanation: For an action already done, "regret" is followed by a noun or by verb + ing: I regret missing your party. "regret miss" and "regret missed" use the wrong form of the verb, and "to missing" mixes "to" with -ing — the common trap is to put "to" after regret.

questions.prompt: Complete the apology: "I'm so sorry ___ I didn't listen to you, Dad."
questions.explanation: "I'm so sorry" is followed by "that" + a full clause (subject + verb): I'm so sorry that I didn't listen to you. "for" and "of" are prepositions and cannot open a clause like "I didn't listen"; "what" is a question word, not a link to a clause.

questions.prompt: Your friend asks: "Why don't we go to the circus?" What is she doing?
questions.explanation: "Why don't we…?" looks like a negative question, but it is one of the openers of a suggestion: she proposes going to the circus. The trap is to read it word by word as "asking for a reason" or as a complaint; nothing in it expresses regret.
